sources.entry: Kodi - Multimedia/Entertainment center, formerly known as XBMC. Runs on Android, BSD, Linux, macOS, iOS and Windows. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 C++/deb

summary.one_liner: Kodi is a free, open source media player and home theater entertainment hub, formerly known as XBMC, that runs on Android, Linux, BSD, macOS, iOS, tvOS and Windows.
summary.what_it_does: Kodi plays most common audio and video formats and is designed for network playback, so it can stream media from elsewhere in the house or from the internet using many protocols. It scans local media and builds a personalized library with box covers, descriptions and fanart. It includes playlist and slideshow functions, a weather forecast feature and audio visualizations. The interface is built for remote-control use from the couch, with a skinning engine for customization. Functionality can be extended with add-ons, which are mainly written in Python and XML, and the core codebase is mainly C++. The project uses CMake as its build system.
use_cases: Home theater media center on a TV
Turning a PC or HTPC into a jukebox
Streaming media from a network share or the internet
Organizing a local movie and music library with artwork
Playing video and audio in almost any format
Extending a media player with add-ons
how_to_run: Download a build for your platform from the downloads section on the Kodi website
Building from source uses CMake; the README points to platform-specific build instructions in the wiki
notable: Formerly known as XBMC, created in 2003 and run as a non-profit by the XBMC Foundation
Extensible through add-ons and a powerful skinning engine
Automatically scans media and builds a library with covers, descriptions and fanart
Available in more than 70 languages through volunteer translators
caveats: Development relies on volunteers, and the README does not describe a support SLA
Build instructions vary by operating system and target platform
